text.p: The board of troubled Victorias Milling Corp has agreed to invite investors to take a stake in the firm, a spokesman for the sugar miller's creditors said on Wednesday.

"The board of Victorias approved a resolution last week to seek stockholder approval at their meeting on May 16 to allow a new capital infusion by a strategic partner," Isidro Alcantara, spokesman of a committee formed by the 32 creditors of Victorias told Reuters.
Victorias had informed the creditors of its board resolution, Alcantara said.
"Stockholders approval is necessary because they have the option of putting up the required money to enable Victorias to turn around its finances," Alcantara said.
Victorias officials were not available for comment.
In earlier interviews, Victorias officials said the firm needed at least two billion pesos in fresh equity.
Alcantara said there had been proposals to sell up to 66 percentof the firm.
Interested buyers in Victorias are local businessman John Gokonwei, Jardine Davies Inc and two unnamed foreign groups, Alcantara said.
Shares of Victorias jumped 65 centavos to 2.85 at the Philippine Stock Exchange today on reports that the sugar miller would soon be put on the auction block, brokers said.

Victorias asked recently for a 90-day moratorium on principal payment of its 4.423 billion pesos debt from 32 foreign and financial institutions due to cashflow problems as a result of a downturn in the local sugar industry.
